summary.text: In physics, work is energy transferred to or from an object when a force acts along a displacement.
For a constant force in the direction of motion, work is force times distance, and its SI unit is the joule.
A force does positive work when it pushes along the motion and negative work when it pushes against it.

items.prompt: A ball is thrown straight up. What sort of work does gravity do on it while it rises?

options.label: Negative, since gravity points against the motion
Positive, since gravity acts on the ball
None, since the ball is moving
Positive, since the ball gains height

items.explain: A force does negative work if it has a component opposite to the displacement.

items.prompt: Lifting a 1-pound weight 4 yards takes the same work as which other lift?

options.label: Lifting 4 pounds 4 yards
Lifting 4 pounds 1 yard
Lifting 1 pound 1 yard
Lifting 2 pounds 1 yard

items.explain: The same work is needed to raise 1 pound 4 yards as 4 pounds 1 yard.

items.prompt: A teacher asks whether work, like force, points in a direction. What is the answer?

options.label: Yes, it points along the force
Yes, it points along the motion
No, it is a scalar with only a size
No, since it has no size at all

items.explain: Work is a scalar quantity, so it has only magnitude and no direction.

items.prompt: A lever lets you lift a heavy rock with a small push. What did Galileo conclude simple machines do?

options.label: They create energy from a small push
They destroy part of the energy of the lifter
They store energy in the rock for later
They transform energy but do not create it

items.explain: Galileo explained that simple machines act as force amplifiers and do not create energy, only transform it.

items.prompt: Why do the SI authorities discourage writing work in newton-metres?

options.label: It gives the wrong size of the unit
It can be confused with a measurement of torque
It cannot be used to measure energy
It only works for forces measured in pounds

items.explain: Newton-metres are dimensionally equivalent but could be mistaken for torque.

items.prompt: You push a stalled car forward a few metres. In physics terms, what has your push done to the car?

options.label: Transferred energy to it
Created energy inside it
Removed energy from it
Stored it in your muscles unchanged

items.explain: Work is energy transferred to or from an object via force along a displacement.
